payload.title: Wedding in Crete Guide to Seasons, Venues and Costs
payload.excerpt: Crete is on your shortlist, and the questions now are practical ones: which month, which end of the island, and what moves the cost. On long-term averages, a wedding in Crete in late spring or early autumn is milder than one in July or August, with few rain days.
key_takeaways: On long-term averages at Heraklion and near Chania, May and September bring highs of about 24 to 27 degrees with few rain days, while most rain falls between October and April.
The east around Elounda and Agios Nikolaos is resort country, while the west centres on the old towns of Chania and Rethymno.
Season, guest rooms, minimum stays, exclusive use and what sits outside a package shape the cost of a Crete wedding.
For a legal wedding, the venue's document deadlines and municipal approval set the shape of the whole planning timeline.

faq.q: When is the best time to get married in Crete?
faq.a: On long-term averages, May and September are milder than high summer with few rain days, and Minos Palace gives April to November as eastern Crete's pleasant window. Beyond that, it depends on the heat and rain you are comfortable with. Long-term averages show almost no rain from June to August, with average highs near or above 30 degrees in the Chania area in July and August. Spring and autumn are the island's mild seasons for touring.

faq.q: Is Crete good for a destination wedding?
faq.a: For many Australian couples, yes. It is the largest island in Greece, with more than 1,000 kilometres of coastline, airports at Heraklion and Chania and a range of venues from resort chapels to hilltop gardens. The trade-offs are summer heat, with July and August highs above 30 degrees in the Chania area, wildfire season from June to September, and a drive of about three hours from Agios Nikolaos to Chania Airport.

faq.q: Which part of Crete is best for a wedding?
faq.a: It comes down to the wedding you want. The east, around Elounda and Agios Nikolaos, is resort country, and Heraklion in the centre keeps its airport close. Chania and Rethymno in the west centre on their old towns, with venues from beach resorts to a hilltop garden. Choose the end of the island by where your guests will land.

faq.q: What affects the cost of a wedding in Crete?
faq.a: Season and date, the rooms and nights a venue asks you to hold, exclusive use, whether you pay a venue fee or a package, extras priced separately and the cost of documents. At the Elounda Collection, official fees are also charged on top of the package rate.

faq.q: Can Australians legally get married in Crete?
faq.a: Yes. Venues such as the Elounda Collection offer civil packages, and there the couple registers the marriage at the Registry Office in Aghios Nikolaos after the ceremony. As at November 2026, a marriage made overseas is usually recognised in Australia if it was valid where it took place and would have been valid under Australian law. Contact the local municipality where you plan to marry for the certificates it requires.

faq.q: How far ahead should we plan a wedding in Crete?
faq.a: Start with the venue's season and work back. Documents for a legal wedding at the Elounda Collection must be issued within 3 months of the date, with copies sent at least 4 weeks and originals at least 3 weeks before. Settle the venue and guest rooms well before that, so the paperwork is the last step rather than the first worry. Ask each venue how far ahead dates in your month are usually taken.
